name: House Targaryen
description: The ruling house of the Seven Kingdoms, bound as much by dragonfire as by blood. King Baelenys' reign has grown harsher since the poisoning, and the loyalty of his own siblings and children has never been so openly tested.

name: House Tyrell
description: Lords of the Reach, whose previous lord — Renrose's father — was executed for his role in the plot to poison King Baelenys alongside Derrin Hightower. The sanctions levied against the house in the aftermath have since been lightened, in part because the Oldtown Massacre shifted the realm's attention and gave Renrose room to quietly rehabilitate his position. He has used that room shrewdly: in secret, he has pledged the full strength of the Reach behind Visenor's claim to the throne in exchange for being named Hand of the King upon his coronation. His first move after sealing the Mander's Pact was to send his fourteen-year-old son Leo to Oldtown, ostensibly to be educated alongside Lady Melessa Hightower. In practice, the boy is Renrose's eyes inside the Hightower — a foothold Visenor has already begun quietly working to limit.

name: House Hightower
description: Once counted among the Crown's most trusted allies through Derrin Hightower's decades as Hand. His secret treason, and the massacre that followed at Oldtown — which claimed young Lord Timos and his sister Alysanne, along with two hundred of the house's knights — has left the house in ruins. The seat now falls to thirteen-year-old Lady Melessa Hightower, who received a wounded and disguised Prince Visenor in her hall and chose to send him on to Highgarden rather than hand him to the Watch. He has since returned — now embedded in the Hightower itself under the alias Maester Arthur Sand, serving as tutor to Melessa and to Leo Tyrell. Only four people within the castle walls know the truth: Melessa, Leo, Ser Martyn Mullendore, and Maester Almar Larchmont.

name: House Stark
description: Wardens of the North, bound to the Iron Throne by an old, uneasy loyalty sealed in blood generations ago. Lord Brandon Stark's death brought his son Rickard to Winterfell's seat, and House Targaryen back to its gates.

name: House Dayne
description: A Dornish house quietly drawn into the heart of the realm's troubles, first through Ser Alester Dayne's sworn service to Prince Jacaelon, then through Lady Lorenah Dayne's decision to shelter a fugitive Crown Prince. Visenor used Starfall's name as cover to enter the Citadel, claiming to be an acolyte sent by Lord Darren Dayne — a lie that has since gone unchallenged.

name: House Velaryon
words: The Old, the True, the Brave
description: Masters of Driftmark and the Crown's oldest maritime allies, tied now to the royal family directly through Naella Velaryon's marriage to Prince Gaelor. Naella carries his heir.

name: House Baratheon
description: Proud stormlanders who fought beside House Targaryen in the past and expect the debt remembered. The Young Stag, Steffon Baratheon, has learned that pride alone does not move a king — though he won the grand tourney by default when neither Targaryen prince could stand.

name: House Vance
description: A lesser house known mainly through Ser Brannyn Vance's service in the Kingsguard, sworn to protect Princess Maela at any cost to himself.

name: House Morrigen
description: A Reach house represented at court by Ser Orwell Morrigen, Lord Commander of the Kingsguard, who watches the realm's unraveling with growing unease.

name: House Lannister
description: Represented at court by Tion Lannister, the Master of Coin, whose sound financial counsel is consistently overruled by princes eager for war.

name: House Blackwood
description: A Riverlands house represented at the grand tourney by Lord Godfrey Blackwood, whose easy charm and open unconventionality made him as memorable off the lists as on them. His quarter-final loss to Jacaelon cost him nothing but pride; his instincts in the semi-finals, when he tackled Brant Costayne mid-assassination, likely saved Prince Gaelor's life.

name: House Mullendore
description: A minor Reach house whose sigil bears butterflies and whose seat lies in the Uplands. House Mullendore has served the Hightowers loyally for generations, and it is through that loyalty that Ser Martyn Mullendore came to recognize a disguised Visenor Targaryen bleeding in an Oldtown alley — and chose to deliver him to Lady Melessa rather than the Watch.

name: House Whent
description: A crownlands house best known here through Curtass Whent, whose long shadow stretched from the Kingsguard to the woods south of King's Landing. Word of his death there, killed in the King's service while hunting Prince Visenor, has since reached the Red Keep — received by the Crown with far more indifference than House Whent might have hoped for.
